scope.cache: fresh private compiler/module caches initially, reused between the two source-identical test processes

profile_interpretation.inuse_space: Sampled heap still in use after the testing package performs end-of-test garbage collection.
profile_interpretation.alloc_space: Sampled cumulative allocation volume during the process, not simultaneous memory demand.
profile_interpretation.allocation_hotspot: s6NewReachingBindingsWithCapacity plus the separate flat allocations in s6CloneReachingBindings account for approximately 61% of allocation volume in each run.

conclusions: Both individual test processes and all four heap analyses completed successfully with normal pressure and no swapping.
Separate process RSS peaks were approximately 8.07 GiB and 7.29 GiB. Profiles retained approximately 3.03 GiB and 2.78 GiB after GC.

The separate runs finished safely and had lower sampled peaks than earlier combined observations, but no valid contemporaneous combined heap profile exists; do not claim a precisely controlled reduction percentage.
About 52.82 GiB and 49.15 GiB cumulative allocation volume indicates substantial test-analysis allocation churn; these values are not required physical RAM.

Allocation profiles identify type-information/AST/binding state and repeated binding clones as concrete optimization targets, while source inspection identifies their cache-retention paths. Profiles alone do not identify GC roots.
Splitting alone still leaves large 7-8 GiB process footprints and does not solve other already-single large test groups or prove old-Mac full-suite viability.
The next bounded change should evaluate coordinated test-only cache lifetimes or avoidable binding-state cloning while retaining cache-correctness and mutation-sensitivity assertions.
No production behavior, test timeout, cache implementation or canonical CI/shard configuration changed in this measurement.
